history.summary: FLAG - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE: Gurdwara Dukh Nivaran Sahib is a Sikh gurdwara - keep-or-drop decision needed. It stands in what was the village of Lehal, now part of Patiala city. Tradition holds that Bhag Ram of Lehal invited Guru Tegh Bahadur (ninth Sikh Guru), who visited on Magh Sudi 5, 1728 Bikram (24 January 1672) and rested under a banyan tree by a pond; the village's mysterious sickness subsided, and the spot was named Dukh Nivaran ('eradicator of suffering'). Devotees revere the sarovar's water for healing qualities. Raja Amar Singh of Patiala (1748-82) laid out a memorial garden entrusted to Nihang Sikhs; in 1920 Maharaja Bhupinder Singh cancelled a railway survey that threatened the banyan tree. A committee formed in 1930 completed construction in 1942; Maharaja Yadavindra Singh built the present building and sarovar. It is administered via the SGPC. NOTE ON DEDUP: this row IS the famous Patiala gurdwara (CSV town Patiala is correct) - it is not a duplicate of itself. It is, however, distinct from CSV row 2037, Gurdwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib in Ludhiana, a separate shrine that shares the name; web sources on that shrine copy the Patiala history onto it (flagged in the 2037 research).
